title: CCPA & California Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to protect your privacy under CCPA and California privacy laws. Exercise your consumer rights and secure your data.
intro: The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA) give you powerful rights to control your personal data. This checklist helps you exercise those rights and implement additional privacy protections specific to California residents.

items.task: Learn your five core CCPA rights
items.why: Understanding your rights is the first step to protecting your privacy under California law.
items.howTo: Review the right to know, delete, opt-out, non-discrimination, and correct your personal information. Bookmark the California Attorney General's CCPA page for reference.

items.task: Identify which businesses must comply with CCPA for your data
items.why: Not all businesses are covered by CCPA - knowing which ones are helps you target your privacy requests effectively.
items.howTo: Look for businesses with $25M+ revenue, 50K+ consumers' data, or 50%+ revenue from selling personal info. Check their privacy policies for CCPA compliance statements.

items.task: Understand what counts as personal information under CCPA
items.why: CCPA has a broad definition of personal information that includes identifiers, browsing history, and inferences about you.
items.howTo: Review the 11 categories of personal information defined by CCPA, including identifiers, commercial information, internet activity, and biometric data.

items.task: Submit requests to know what personal information companies have
items.why: You have the right to know what personal information businesses collect, use, and share about you.
items.howTo: Use company privacy portals or submit written requests. Ask for categories and specific pieces of personal information, sources, business purposes, and third parties they share with.

items.task: Opt out of the sale of your personal information
items.why: CCPA requires businesses to provide a 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' link and honor your opt-out request.
items.howTo: Look for 'Do Not Sell' links on websites, usually in footers. Submit opt-out requests to major data collectors like Google, Facebook, and data brokers.

items.task: Request deletion of your personal information
items.why: You can request businesses delete your personal information, with some exceptions for business operations.
items.howTo: Submit deletion requests through privacy portals or contact forms. Be specific about what data you want deleted and follow up to confirm completion.

items.task: Request correction of inaccurate personal information
items.why: Under CPRA, you have the right to correct inaccurate personal information that businesses maintain about you.
items.howTo: Contact businesses directly when you find inaccurate information in your data reports. Provide correct information and request they update their records.

items.task: Identify data brokers that may have your information
items.why: Data brokers collect and sell personal information, often without direct consumer interaction.
items.howTo: Check the California Attorney General's data broker registry. Research major brokers like Acxiom, Epsilon, Experian, and LexisNexis Risk Solutions.

items.task: Submit opt-out requests to major data brokers
items.why: Data brokers must honor CCPA opt-out requests and stop selling your personal information.
items.howTo: Visit each data broker's website to find their CCPA opt-out process. Many require identity verification. Consider using automated services to streamline this process.

items.task: Limit use of sensitive personal information
items.why: CPRA gives you the right to limit how businesses use sensitive personal information like Social Security numbers and precise location data.
items.howTo: Look for 'Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information' links on websites. Submit requests to businesses that collect sensitive data about you.

items.task: Use Incognito Browser for enhanced privacy protection
items.why: While CCPA gives you rights, proactive protection prevents data collection in the first place.
items.howTo: Download Incognito Browser which blocks trackers and prevents behavioral profiling. This reduces the amount of data companies can collect about your online activities.

items.why: GPC automatically communicates your opt-out preferences to websites, making CCPA compliance easier.
items.howTo: Enable GPC in privacy-focused browsers or install browser extensions that send GPC signals. California law requires businesses to honor these automated signals.

items.task: Monitor business compliance with your CCPA requests
items.why: Businesses must respond to CCPA requests within 45 days and actually implement the changes you request.
items.howTo: Keep records of all privacy requests and responses. Follow up if businesses don't respond within 45 days or fail to honor your requests. File complaints with the California Attorney General if needed.

items.task: Regularly review privacy policies of services you use
items.why: CCPA requires businesses to disclose their data practices, giving you insight into how your information is used.
items.howTo: Check privacy policies for CCPA disclosures about data collection, use, and sharing. Look for information about retention periods and your rights as a California resident.
